pr_title: Add centroid grid type in mvt request
pr_body:
This PR adds a new grid type called centroid. When users selects this grid type, the the features on the aggregation layer are represented by a point that is computed from the centroid of the data inside the cell. It might happen for complex geometries that the actual centroid is out of the cell, in that case the point is the closes point inside the cell to the centroid.

closes #77215

issue_context.title: Use centroid for location of clusters when using grid_type `point` in mvt requests
issue_context.body:
The `point`-setting for `grid_type` places the cluster in the center of the grid-cell. 

This creates some visual artefacts which do not look natural.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1833023/131904927-8337aa5e-ae35-4447-bfc6-c0dff669a01f.png)

Having the user to increase the `grid_resolution` is not the right work-around for many use-cases. While, this may place the clusters in a more accurate location, it also creates a lot more clusters in the response. Especially when symbolizing these clusters, the symbol will be larger than the grid-cell in pixel-size, resulting in a messy visualization.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1833023/131904296-f91210e7-3185-4d02-83d0-6f8c03340345.png)


cc @iverase

review_comments: This is the logic to make sure the point is always inside the cell.
Maybe add an explanation why it is invalid (like aggregations cannot start with `_mvt`)
It is not allowed to use '[' or ']' in the name of aggregations using the rest interface so calling like this prevents name collision.
That looks a bit hack-y. I wonder if we would be better off by adding a special prefix to all internal aggs and prohibiting external aggs to use this prefix in their names?

I agree, it looks like a bug that the rest interface does not allow that construct but you do it in java. 

My first idea was to add a prefix to the user defined aggregations so we do not need to add any restriction but it seems that would be pretty invasive as at the moment there is no tooling for doing that. 

We can add a prefix to the internal aggs, let say they should start with an underscore '_' and the API fails if a user sends an aggregation which name starts with that prefix. @thomasneirynck would that be an issue for you?
I think if we pick `_mvt_` or something like that, it would have much less chances to conflict with anything.
